name: Negentropic Field
description: The tendency of living systems to spontaneously organize rather than dissolve. Measured by M(S) = (R_e · A · D) − L, where geometric resonance, adaptability, and diversity overcome loss. Grounded in Fokker-Planck dynamics where reducing diffusion triggers probability collapse into coherent states.

core_attributes.pattern: self-organization, entropy reversal, phase transition coherence

scope.definition: Magnitude of local entropy reduction achievable in living systems — ratio of information content accumulated in a mature ecosystem (bits per unit volume) to thermodynamically maximum entropy for same matter at same temperature.

evidence.source: Schrödinger (1944) 'What is Life?', Cambridge UP; Prigogine (1977) Nobel Lecture 'Time, structure and fluctuations'; Deacon (2011) 'Incomplete Nature', W.W. Norton.
cross_domain_examples: living cells maintain 10⁸-10¹⁰ bits of genetic and epigenetic information per cell — vs thermal equilibrium maximum
coral reef ecosystem: structural complexity representing 10³ bits/cm³ above thermodynamic equilibrium baseline
Prigogine dissipative structures: local entropy reduction mathematically proven possible under energy throughput

scope.falsifiability: If life is found that does not require continuous energy throughput to maintain its organized state, the dissipative structure model (local negentropy requires energy flow) fails.
scope.measurement_limits: Negentropy is a useful concept but has no single operational definition — different formalisms give different numerical values. The 0.96 reflects living systems' capacity to approach maximum local information content, not a single measurement.
